GRANITE SPIRE CLUSTER: four sheer granite spires rising from a broken talus field, their faces streaked rust and silver where iron seams run vertical, a belt of twisted conifers at irregular spacing clinging to ledges two-thirds up, loose boulders the size of houses piled at their feet

GLACIATED MASSIF: a broad massif of pale blue-grey gneiss carrying three glaciers in its upper cirques, arêtes dividing the snowfields into sharp fins, hanging valleys notched into the flanks, a rubble moraine apron spreading across the lower slope where sparse larch stand at uneven spacing

VOLCANIC CONE: a symmetrical andesite cone rising steep from a forested piedmont, its upper third bare grey scree streaked with sulphur-yellow mineral staining, a rim of fractured lava blocks at the summit, dense mixed forest of uneven girth wrapping the lower slopes in dark green

KNIFE-EDGE RIDGE: a serrated quartzite arête running two miles across the skyline, its crest chipped into gendarmes and notches by frost action, the east face dropping sheer to a cirque lake, the west face a long steep ramp of angular rubble with sparse alpine sedge tucked in cracks

RED SLOT CANYON: a narrow winding canyon of deep rust and cream sandstone, walls sculpted into smooth undulating waves and horizontal ribs by water over millennia, the floor a strip of pale fine sand, the walls curving inward and nearly touching two hundred feet overhead

LAYERED RED CANYON: a wide canyon of alternating brick-red, ochre, and cream sedimentary strata, each layer of differing hardness carving its own ledge or overhang, buttes and pinnacles standing free on the mid-level terraces, a thin green riparian strip along the canyon bottom

RIVER GORGE: a deep river gorge cut through dark grey basalt and older granite, its walls nearly vertical for four hundred feet, horizontal jointing splitting the rock into clean slabs, a white-water river filling the full gorge floor, scattered ferns rooting in damp cracks along the lower walls

NORTHERN FJORD COAST: a deep fjord of dark water flanked by walls of bare grey schist rising a thousand metres straight from the waterline, a U-shaped valley profile overhead, a delta fan of grey gravel at the head, birch scrub at irregular spacing on the lower talus slopes

SEA STACK HEADLAND: a basalt headland stepping down into a series of black columnar sea stacks standing off a dark pebble shore, their flat tops capped with wind-flattened grass and sea-pink, surf breaking white around their angular bases, the headland cliff face streaked white with mineral seepage

GRANITE SEA CLIFF: a sheer pink granite sea cliff running a kilometre of coast, vertical crack systems splitting it into broad panels, the clifftop a thin mat of coastal heath at irregular height, loose blocks of exfoliated granite resting at the cliff base in the intertidal zone

CHALK CLIFFS: a long face of bright white chalk running in a gentle curve, each layer of flint nodules forming a dark horizontal band across the face, the clifftop carrying a mat of short turf and scattered hawthorn of uneven girth, the cliff base a sloping ramp of chalk rubble

FJORD WATERFALL WALL: a fjord wall of layered dark gabbro and lighter granite intrusions, three hanging valleys spilling waterfalls at different heights down the same face, the rock face wet and dark below each cascade, cushion moss and fern occupying every damp ledge down to the waterline

DUNE SEA: a vast sea of crescent barchans and star dunes in orange and buff quartz sand, the slip faces crisp and sharp-edged, the windward flanks smooth and gradual, occasional yardangs of dark indurated sandstone protruding through the sand between dune corridors

SALT FLAT: a vast flat of white halite crust cracked into a mosaic of polygons a metre across, the crust thickening toward the centre where salt ridges buckle upward, a fringe of dark mudflat at the margins where gypsum crystals grow in clusters at the surface

BADLANDS: an eroded landscape of grey and purple bentonite clay carved into a dense maze of hoodoos and sharp ridges, the clay layers banded in ochre, lavender, and olive, cap rocks of harder sandstone balancing on narrowed pedestals, sparse clumps of rabbitbrush rooting in the harder seams

BLACK LAVA COAST: a coast of recent pahoehoe lava in glossy black basalt, its surface folded into rope-like coils and pressure ridges, older flows behind it weathering to dull grey with a thin crust of pale lichen, sparse ohia trees of uneven girth and lean pushing through cracks in the older rock

CALDERA LAKE: a caldera of layered rhyolite and ash tuff forming a near-circular rim, the inner walls dropping steeply to a deep blue-green crater lake, the rim crest fractured into blocky outcrops, sparse lodgepole pine of irregular spacing and girth occupying the outer caldera slope

ICE SHELF EDGE: the seaward edge of a continental ice shelf, the face a vertical wall of stratified blue-white glacial ice sixty metres tall, pressure ridges and seracs rising above the flat shelf surface behind it, the ice face fractured into angular blocks and overhanging cornices along its length

GLACIER TONGUE: a valley glacier tongue of blue-grey ice pushing into a moraine-dammed lake, the ice surface ridged with medial moraines of dark rock debris running its full length, crevasse fields opening across the lower tongue, lateral moraines of unsorted boulders and gravel flanking both sides

TERRACED HILLSIDE: a steep hillside of volcanic basalt carved into broad agricultural terraces of dark green, each terrace wall of stacked dry stone, the hillside profile stepping back in a series of flat shelves, irregular fig and olive trees of uneven girth and lean scattered across the upper terraces

ROLLING CHALK HILLS: a landscape of smooth rounded chalk hills in long sweeping curves, the turf close-cropped and pale green over the thin chalky soil, copses of beech at irregular spacing and uneven age sitting in the combes between ridges, the hilltops bare and rounded against each other

BRAIDED RIVER VALLEY: a wide glacial outwash valley floor laced with braided river channels of grey glacial meltwater, gravel bars of polished schist and granite between channels, willows of irregular height and spacing rooting on the more stable bars, the valley walls of bare glacially smoothed granite rising steeply on each side

HIGHLAND PLATEAU: a flat-topped plateau of dark sandstone at high elevation, its surface a mosaic of exposed rock pavement and peat bog, the plateau edge breaking into a series of stepped cliffs exposing horizontal strata in rust and tan, scattered stunted pine of uneven lean occupying the sheltered plateau edge

VOLCANIC ISLAND: a single basaltic island rising steep from the ocean, its slopes of dark weathered lava terraced by ancient lava benches at different sea levels, the upper cone of bare scoria and cinder in red and black, dense tropical forest of irregular canopy and girth wrapping the mid-slopes

MOUNTAIN LAKE BASIN: a deep lake filling a glacially scoured basin of pale granite, the basin walls polished smooth by ice and striated with horizontal grooves, a terminal moraine of unsorted boulders forming the lake's lower shore, scattered old pine and larch of irregular girth leaning on the lower basin walls
